sources.title: OOTP official wiki — Creating Games
sources.observed: The official manual separates standard, custom, historical, advanced and quick-start creation paths. It describes a wizard for custom setup and identifies advanced mode as a separate route.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: make the mode decision explicit, then expose only the settings relevant to that mode; end on a review sheet.
sources.avoid: Do not import OOTP's MLB modes, historical database or automatic management systems into PAWA.
sources.evidenceType: Official manual text opened 2026-09-18; documented workflow, not a hands-on test.

sources.title: Football Manager 26 — Reimagined User Interface
sources.observed: FM describes a Portal combining home and inbox, task/unread filters, an action panel, grouped top navigation, and bookmarks. Tiles open more detailed cards. The article says readability and platform-specific screens shaped the redesign.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: separate actionable messages from unread messages; reveal secondary detail on demand; give the game menu named destination groups.
sources.avoid: Do not copy the universal tile system. PAWA needs distinct page composition rather than the same cards everywhere.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer feature text opened 2026-09-18; claims describe design intent, not proof of usability.

sources.title: OOTP official wiki — History Index
sources.observed: The history index begins with seasons and finalists, emphasizes the champion, and links years to team history. Separate destinations cover players, teams, managers, leaderboards, awards and accomplishments.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: use stable year/category coordinates and evidence links so archive exploration cannot be confused with the live league.
sources.avoid: Do not copy the full nested link hierarchy or assume historical information exists when PAWA snapshots lack it.
sources.evidenceType: Official manual text opened 2026-09-18; information architecture evidence, not a current in-game screenshot audit.

sources.title: NBA 2K25 — MyNBA and MyGM Courtside Report
sources.observed: 2K describes fewer, more consequential MyGM conversations; historical news presentation changes from newspaper to web formats and social feeds. The report also describes simplifying staff management.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: make weekly news an editorial issue, live activity a compact stream, and narrative decisions a focused scene. Different content deserves different reading rhythm.
sources.avoid: Do not add walkable offices, invented NPC conversations, era simulation or unsupported role-playing effects.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer report opened 2026-09-18; documented content and presentation patterns, not hands-on validation.

sources.title: EA College Football 26 — Dynasty and Team Builder Deep Dive
sources.observed: EA describes choosing an existing coach or creating one. Its Trophy Room records achievements with season, team, score or individual recipient context; selecting a trophy exposes more information.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: coach setup should foreground identity and supported tradeoffs; awards should present recipients with the actual season and achievement evidence.
sources.avoid: Do not borrow licensed marks, imply PAWA has EA's coach progression, or turn every statistical record into a trophy.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer article and accompanying image descriptions opened 2026-09-18; no game session or video playthrough.

screens.composition: One campus vista fills the frame; a narrow vertical play menu sits in intentional empty sky/dugout space. Last accessible dynasty is a single subtitle under Continue.
screens.primaryDecision: Resume a specific dynasty or begin another journey.
screens.interaction: Arrow keys and pointer choose menu items; Continue names its target before navigation.
screens.compact: Keep the vertical menu over a quiet solid-backed crop; account control stays at top.
screens.difference: An atmospheric entry with four destinations, not a working league dashboard.
unapprovedDependencies: Final campus key art; no animated environment or controller support implied.

screens.composition: A single compact credential sheet floats over a muted entrance crop. Show the intended league destination above the form.
screens.primaryDecision: Sign in and return to the intended destination.
remove: Account marketing and duplicate sign-in controls
screens.interaction: Submit once; retain non-secret identity input on failure; route only after confirmed success.
screens.compact: Full-width form, visible Back, keyboard-safe spacing; no side panels.
screens.difference: A short authentication task rather than a game menu.

screens.composition: One linear registration sheet uses three visual bands: account identity, credentials, and creation consequence. Invite context remains a small header.
screens.primaryDecision: Create the account required to own the requested session.
screens.interaction: Validate beside fields; preserve valid entries after rejection; creation is a single named action.
screens.compact: One column with text labels; errors precede the submit action.
screens.difference: Account creation stays distinct from coach customization.

screens.composition: A short guest pass contains the real persistence limitation followed by two stacked choices. Avoid a second onboarding funnel.
screens.primaryDecision: Enter as a guest with known limits or create an account.
screens.interaction: The guest action begins one session request; warning remains visible while pending.
screens.compact: Two full-width labeled buttons below the consequence sentence.
screens.difference: A deliberate temporary-access fork; not another form.

screens.composition: One full-width list of dynasty spines: name, team mark, mode, current phase and last activity. The last played entry is taller; each entry owns its Continue action. Tools live behind a labeled library command.
screens.primaryDecision: Choose which world to resume.
remove: KPI cards copied from the active league
screens.interaction: Choose a save directly; a contextual menu handles details/deletion separately from Continue.
screens.compact: Vertical save spines retain name, phase and primary action; no carousel.
screens.difference: A library of worlds with no need to open a generic inspector first.

screens.composition: A full-width step sequence shows Mode, Competition, Sources and Review. One task owns the center at a time; completed decisions become a collapsible summary ribbon.
screens.primaryDecision: Create the exact reviewed simulation or companion world.
screens.interaction: Back preserves selections; choosing a mode reveals relevant supported fields; Create occurs only on the review step.
screens.compact: Single step with top Back/step label and readable next action, never four squeezed columns.
screens.difference: A narrowing decision sequence rather than a configurable dashboard.
unapprovedDependencies: Step draft persistence across reload requires implementation; do not promise it.

screens.composition: Conference headings divide a full-width school ballot. Each row shows monogram, name, selected state and relevant eligibility. A top count explains required versus chosen teams.
screens.primaryDecision: Confirm a valid competition field.
screens.interaction: Toggle eligible schools; constraint feedback names the blocking rule; confirmation reviews totals.
screens.compact: Conference selector plus checked rows; selected count remains above the list.
screens.difference: A multi-select competition ballot, not scouting or team comparison.

screens.composition: A large cel coach and selected school mark form a media-day backdrop; one focused foreground form progresses from school to identity to existing skill allocation.
screens.primaryDecision: Commit to the coach and school combination.
remove: Cosmetic controls that imply unsupported bonuses
screens.interaction: Preview permitted identity changes; claim/save only after confirming current availability and valid allocation.
screens.compact: Portrait becomes a compact header; each form stage uses full width.
screens.difference: Identity gets a character-creation moment rather than an admin record editor.
unapprovedDependencies: Production cel customization kit; no new archetypes, perks or appearance mechanics.

screens.composition: A prominent league masthead leads into school/coach seat rows. A separate readiness strip summarizes class, schedule and assignments. The commissioner Start action follows its exact blockers.
screens.primaryDecision: Claim an available school or resolve the blocker preventing league start.
remove: Decorative scene above all useful content
screens.interaction: Selecting an open seat opens only its claim flow; start is role-aware and rechecks prerequisites.
screens.compact: Rollcall becomes stacked seat rows; readiness appears before the final start control.
screens.difference: A social readiness room with named occupants, not a general operations console.
unapprovedDependencies: Any presence display needs actual freshness data; no chat or synchronized avatar lobby.

screens.composition: A slim vertical stage timeline sits beside the reviewed creation name. Completed/current/failed stages have explicit text; the final successful state replaces progress with Enter dynasty.
screens.primaryDecision: Wait, enter the confirmed world, or follow the supported recovery path.
remove: Campus construction implying real facility progression
screens.interaction: Revisit the same operation identity after navigation; show retry only when supported.
screens.compact: One stage stack and one status action; details expand downward.
screens.difference: A receipt for one operation, not a loading dashboard.
unapprovedDependencies: Resumption/retry only if creation API supports it; no new recovery guarantee.

screens.composition: A single invitation letter names the league, intended role if known, and current account. Acceptance and account switching are distinct actions below the identity check.
screens.primaryDecision: Join this league as the displayed account.
remove: Raw token displayed as decorative code
screens.interaction: Accept once; preserve invitation context across sign-in; an existing member gets Open league.
screens.compact: One readable letter with actions below; no league navigation until authorized.
screens.difference: A membership decision, not a miniature league home.

screens.composition: A full-width statistical ledger gets a two-line control header: season/scope, then batting/pitching and metric preset. The leading row has restrained emphasis; player details open only on demand.
screens.primaryDecision: Which performance ranks highest under this scope and qualification?
remove: Decorative KPI totals repeating table columns
screens.interaction: Sorting changes the named order; choose a row for a full profile and return to the same sort/position.
screens.compact: Keep rank, athlete, selected metric and sample in view; switch metric groups instead of shrinking every column.
screens.difference: A comparison instrument that devotes nearly all width to aligned evidence.

screens.composition: A category index opens a typeset record page: value and holder first, then tied holders, team/year and source link. Single-season and career scope sit above the record list.
screens.primaryDecision: Which achievement and holder should I inspect?
screens.interaction: Open a record category, select the record, follow its archived evidence; Back retains category.
screens.compact: Category selector opens one record page with tied holders stacked.
screens.difference: An achievement reference book, distinct from sorting current-season statistics.
unapprovedDependencies: Do not infer all-time records from incomplete archives.

screens.composition: A visible year index leads to a season contents page. The selected year is stamped across the masthead; chapters open full-width historical tables or spreads.
screens.primaryDecision: Which completed season and chapter do I want to revisit?
keep: Links to archived teams and fixtures
remove: All chapters simultaneously in dashboard cards
screens.interaction: Year first, chapter second; preserve both in navigation and clearly mark any link back to live data.
screens.compact: Year chooser and chapter list replace a permanent rail; one chapter owns the screen.
screens.difference: A historical container organized by year, not the live league page tinted sepia.

screens.composition: A single team-season masthead leads into a historical roster register with chapter switches for recorded results and honors. The year remains beside the team name everywhere.
screens.primaryDecision: Inspect this team as it existed in that year.
remove: Current roster silently filling snapshot gaps
screens.interaction: Historical players open a read-only snapshot view; Live team is a separately labeled exit.
screens.compact: One register section at a time; each detail keeps team and year at top.
screens.difference: A frozen team volume rather than a live profile with an archive badge.

screens.composition: One issue uses an editorial lead headline, compact result rail and two supporting columns of factual briefs. Required decisions appear in a clearly labeled box, not inside celebratory copy. Issue navigation is a top date chooser.
screens.primaryDecision: What materially changed this week, and what needs my attention?
screens.interaction: Read the issue in priority order; open a source or task without marking it resolved merely by reading.
screens.compact: One-column newspaper order: lead, decisions, results, supporting briefs.
screens.difference: A curated weekly edition, unlike the raw ticker or personal inbox.
unapprovedDependencies: Editorial prioritization must use available events; no fabricated quotes or generated facts.

screens.composition: A stationary chronological wire groups compact events by date/week. Category chips sit above the stream; new events collect behind a count button rather than moving existing rows.
screens.primaryDecision: Which recent event deserves inspection?
screens.interaction: Open event inline or follow its linked record; manually reveal newer items and retain reading position.
screens.compact: Single event column with filters in a named sheet; no sideways ticker.
screens.difference: A low-friction activity log rather than another editorial homepage.
unapprovedDependencies: New-event count requires supported polling/event updates; do not imply live sockets.

screens.composition: A narrow message queue shares the page with one full reading sheet. Two top filters independently distinguish unread from unresolved; any valid action lives at the end of the actual message.
screens.primaryDecision: Read or act on the selected coach message.
screens.interaction: Select message, read context, then follow its action. Archive remains a separate command and never resolves the underlying task.
screens.compact: Queue and reader become two screens; Back restores selection and filters.
screens.difference: A personal correspondence workflow; the only deliberate list-reader split in this group.
unapprovedDependencies: Unresolved filter requires reliable task-state linkage; otherwise keep supported categories.

screens.composition: One active arc opens as a story spread with a scene headline, factual context, participants and a small consequence timeline. Eligible choices/votes sit beneath the context. Intel and commissioner tools are separate chapters.
screens.primaryDecision: Choose a supported story action or vote with its known consequences.
remove: Invented dialogue or implied hidden rewards
screens.interaction: Read context before selecting a choice; confirmation names the option; expired/completed decisions become read-only history.
screens.compact: Context then choices then history; no side panel holding required information.
screens.difference: A focused narrative decision, not a news list with a vote widget.
unapprovedDependencies: New dialogue, branching outcomes or artwork require separate design approval; use existing story content.

screens.composition: There is no new designed destination. Replace the retired route with its accessible league hub; only a brief fallback names the current destination.
screens.primaryDecision: Continue to the current Matchday brief.
remove: Loading scene or new War Room branding
screens.interaction: Replace navigation history so Back does not loop; failed access uses the normal recovery state.
screens.compact: Same redirect; no separate phone design.
screens.difference: A compatibility route deliberately receives no new screen.

screens.composition: One calm recovery page names the problem in plain language, offers an accessible hub when known, and always offers Dynasty selection. A small neutral diamond illustration is optional.
screens.primaryDecision: Choose a safe known destination.
remove: Raw route tokens or stack traces
Fake retry for permanently missing content
screens.interaction: Use one destination action; retry appears only for recoverable loading/network errors, not arbitrary 404s.
screens.compact: Short text and two full-width actions; no decorative scrolling page.
screens.difference: Recovery is a plain decision surface, not a disabled version of the normal dashboard.

screens.composition: Conference groups form one aligned standings ledger. The user team has a subtle row marker; any supported qualification boundary is labeled in the table itself.
screens.primaryDecision: Where does the program stand in the official race?
keep: Official record and games back where supported
screens.interaction: Choose conference, inspect a team, return to the same standings position.
screens.compact: Team, W-L and supported rank/GB remain primary; additional columns use metric presets.
screens.difference: A race table aligned by teams, unlike individual stat leaders or ranking opinions.

screens.composition: A conference-organized directory of compact school nameplates fills the page. Selecting Compare opens a new two-program sheet with equal columns and matched metric periods.
screens.primaryDecision: Find a program or compare two named programs.
remove: Composite power score invented for visual impact
screens.interaction: Choose first and second program explicitly; compare is a separate route/state, with Swap and Clear.
screens.compact: Directory stays a list; comparison shows labeled A/B values per metric group.
screens.difference: A navigable program directory that changes composition only when comparison is requested.
unapprovedDependencies: Comparison state and return behavior need implementation; no new composite metric.

screens.composition: A dated ranking release leads with week and source, followed by current rank, prior rank and movement in one full-width ordered list. New entrants use text, not a false delta.
screens.primaryDecision: How did this published ranking change?
remove: Standings record presented as ranking authority
screens.interaction: Switch published week only where snapshots exist; open the ranked program for context.
screens.compact: Rank, team and movement form one readable line with a secondary record line.
screens.difference: A published ordered snapshot rather than the competition standings table.
unapprovedDependencies: Historical ranking selection requires retained snapshots; absent methodology stays unexplained, not invented.

screens.composition: Award categories form restrained cabinet headings. One selected honor gets recipient portrait, award name and season; other recipients remain a compact roll of honor below.
screens.primaryDecision: Inspect the actual recipient and achievement.
screens.interaction: Select category or recipient; open the actual player/season evidence. Do not trigger celebration for unawarded honors.
screens.compact: Award selector plus one featured recipient and roll of honor.
screens.difference: An achievement ceremony surface distinct from record lookup or raw leaders.
unapprovedDependencies: Original award silhouette/portrait assets; avoid EA trophies and licensed designs.

screens.composition: A chronological season ledger shows year, champion and the few retained major outcomes. The main interaction is selecting a year; rich reading happens in Archive.
screens.primaryDecision: Which season should I open?
remove: Mini charts without consistent historical data
screens.interaction: Select a year to open its archive, not a separate competing history dashboard.
screens.compact: Stacked season rows with champion and Open year.
screens.difference: A concise index into Archive; it is not an additional archival content system.

screens.composition: Date groups contain factual edit entries with actor, affected record and correction summary. Opening an entry reveals authorized before/after values directly below it.
screens.primaryDecision: What changed, and which record is affected?
remove: Audit data exposed as social news
screens.interaction: Expand one event inline or open its record; unavailable/restricted detail is labeled.
screens.compact: One event column; before and after stack with explicit labels.
screens.difference: A correction journal with precise provenance, separate from the public activity wire.
unapprovedDependencies: Do not reconstruct missing before/after values or expose private scouting through logs.

screens.composition: A season cover names the final record and completed year. A deliberate reading sequence follows: results, actual honors, departing players and arrivals. Each chapter ends with its archive evidence link.
screens.primaryDecision: Review what the completed season meant and continue when ready.
screens.interaction: Next/previous chapter and contents list remain available; Exit returns without advancing league state.
screens.compact: One chapter per view with a persistent year label and clear contents control.
screens.difference: An end-of-season reading experience, while Archive remains the searchable reference.
unapprovedDependencies: Scrapbook export, new generated narration and share layouts remain unapproved dependencies.

screens.composition: The shell supplies a small league/season/status band, then yields most space to each page's own composition. A top Menu opens grouped text destinations over the paused interface; preferences are a separate sheet.
screens.primaryDecision: Navigate to a named area or resume the current task.
remove: Global workspace plus mandatory sidebar on every screen
Bottom tab bar or unexplained icon-only destinations
screens.interaction: Open menu, choose group/destination, or Escape back to the exact invoking control; never discard dirty input silently.
screens.compact: A top Menu opens a full-screen named destination list; no bottom navigation.
screens.difference: The shell is a navigation layer, not the composition template for every screen.
unapprovedDependencies: Controller mapping, bookmarks, audio assets and persistent preference behavior require their own implementation/approval.
